---
title: "Architecture"
doc-type: explanation
---

`repo-familiar` is organized around a Project Generator, a canonical Reference Source, and self-contained Downstream Repositories. The architecture favors inspectable copies and explicit ownership over hidden synchronization.

## Product Boundary

The primary product is repository generation and guarded adoption, not workstation setup. The Reference Source owns reusable templates, profile registries, selectable skills, command behavior, and documentation conventions. A Downstream Repository receives selected assets and then remains independently maintainable.

Machine-level harness configuration, global MCP settings, shell setup, credentials, and secret stores remain user-owned. Repository guidance may describe them but generation does not silently mutate them.

## Vendored Assets And Provenance

Generated assets are copied into downstream repositories. This makes each repository stable if the Reference Source later changes, and it lets downstream maintainers edit local files deliberately.

Bootstrap Metadata v1 records provenance, selections, generated paths, and checksums. Schema v2 adds render context, Managed Surfaces, and operation history. `.repo-familiar/` is generator-owned metadata; `.agents/` contains agent-facing runtime instructions and guidance.

Checksums do not make generated files immutable. They establish a comparison baseline so checks and promotions can distinguish unchanged, edited, missing, adopted, and conflicting content.

## Preview-First Change

New generation writes a new repository after optional dry-run review. Existing-repository bootstrap, targeted additions, upgrades, metadata migration, attachment, and promotion separate preview from apply.

This asymmetry is intentional: a new empty output has no user history, while an existing repository has unknown ownership and local decisions. Missing or checksum-clean content can be eligible for narrow writes; edits and ambiguity fail closed for review.

Managed Surface promotion is atomic at the selected boundary. Broad template promotion is dependency-ordered and changes the recorded template only after all target surfaces conform. There is no live or background sync.

## Template Composition

Concrete templates compose known layers internally while Bootstrap Metadata records the effective template and per-file source. `python-reproducible` is the greenfield default; `basic` remains the generic template and conservative existing-repository fallback; `static-quarto-application` adds an explicit browser-to-API product boundary.

A Static Quarto Application is not another documentation mode. Its static browser client initiates ordinary FastAPI request/response calls, while project documentation remains a Divio Quarto site under `docs/`.

## Engineering Opinions

- Prefer executable evidence over prose-only claims: manifests, locks, tests, CI, provenance, and tutorial verification should describe the same path.
- Introduce dependencies when the scaffold exercises them or a documented threshold is met, not because they appear in a preferred stack list.
- Use `uv` for Python package and environment management.
- Use Pydantic at validation boundaries, Polars for dataframe work, and Hamilton where graph-shaped execution benefits from inspectable DAGs.
- Reserve FastAPI and Structlog for service/application boundaries that need them.
- Introduce Banks, Hydra/OmegaConf, and remote-storage abstractions only when template complexity, configuration composition, or storage requirements justify them.
- Keep safety, privacy, accessibility, inclusion, and maintainability visible as product requirements rather than optional review passes.

## Source Boundaries

Canonical templates and `src/repo_familiar/asset_plan.py` define generated composition. `src/repo_familiar/metadata.py` defines Bootstrap Metadata. `src/repo_familiar/profiles.py` defines profile registries. `src/repo_familiar/advice.py` detects repository signals and orchestrates pure recommendation nodes from `src/repo_familiar/advice_dag.py`.

Use the [Repository Map](../project-record/repository-map.md) for ownership and focused tests, [Bootstrap Lifecycle](../reference/bootstrap-lifecycle.qmd) for exact command safety, and ADRs for durable rationale.

Deterministic example snapshots are regression fixtures for this architecture. They should be regenerated from canonical inputs rather than edited by hand.
